calls.head: Strength vs. Strength
calls.body: The Oilers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kings are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Kings’ defense.
calls.call: The Kings keep the Oilers’ chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot).

calls.head: The Oilers’ power play is a weapon
calls.body: On the power play, Edmonton is the league’s best, but Los Angeles is near the bottom. Every penalty the Kings take could cost them. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates more per 60 than the Kings’.

LAK.head: We had Los Angeles as slight underdogs (42%), and it went Edmonton’s way.

EDM.head: We leaned Edmonton’s way (58%), and they came through.

surprises.head: Los Angeles took away the good looks
surprises.body: Los Angeles is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Edmonton’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (about 6.2% against Los Angeles) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Four points for McDavid as the Oilers beat the Kings
paras: Leon Draisaitl and Vasily Podkolzin scored a minute apart early in the first to put the Oilers up 2-0. Connor McDavid made it 3-0 late in the period, in his 800th NHL game. Los Angeles pulled Darcy Kuemper after three goals and turned to Anton Forsberg to start the second. Brandt Clarke got the Kings on the board late in the second, and Podkolzin struck again into the empty net with a little over two minutes left. McDavid finished with four points on a goal and three assists.
The score flatters the Oilers: the Kings had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Kings win about six in ten. Devon Levi was the difference, stopping 39 of 40.

The Oilers killed all four Kings power plays. The Oil moved to 5-0-1, still first in the NHL in points percentage. The Kings are seventh in the Pacific. The Kings are still looking for their first win of the season, now 0-3-2.

items.text: The Oilers are rolling: five straight wins.
Vasily Podkolzin has a point in every game this season, with a goal in each of the last three.
Leon Draisaitl extended his point streak against Los Angeles to seven games.
Brandt Clarke scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 2 (26 games played since).
